links.outcome: Alert burden of sepsis prediction alerts per non-ICU patient days after deployment
links.effect: 264 alerts on 173 patients; 10 alerts per 1000 non-ICU patient days per month; 89% bedside huddle completion; no special cause variation in days between sepsis-attributable emergent transfers.
links.quote: An automated electronic health record-based sepsis prediction model, CDS tools, and sepsis huddle workflows were implemented on inpatient units with a relatively low rate of interruptive alerts and high compliance with bedside huddles.

unlisted_practices: Using simulation and safety science methods to proactively analyze and refine CDS tools and workflows before implementation
Rapid PDSA cycles using user feedback and weekly metric data during rollout
Bedside sepsis huddle workflow triggered by predictive alerts

screen.reason: The study evaluates the real-world deployment of an EHR sepsis prediction model combined with safety science/simulation workflows and iterative PDSA cycles, monitoring huddle compliance and alert rates.

primary.practice: simulation-guided workflow design and rapid PDSA cycles for CDS deployment
